columns: paragraph: Scan 034
row: The raised star is commonly a small angular k-like mark (I*, I′*, φ*) rather than a symmetric asterisk. It holds at the clear occurrences on this sheet; the crowded inline target has an additional unresolved mark. I has heavy top and bottom bars, while J has a left-curved foot: the apparent doubled stroke on the upper J′ is retracing, not evidence for a separate alphabet. Both witnesses retain ordinary capitals. The shorthand = after “Mais” consists of two horizontal strokes and stands where “même” would read naturally; C offered si and H omitted it. The long descenders of j and f can resemble a cancellation: H took the live “p bijectif” as struck. These are page-local observations to compare on subsequent sheets.

columns: paragraph: Scan 035
row: The subdivision sign has a curved wedge and lower curve, distinct from the ordinary ≤ used later; C flattened both opening occurrences. Latin f, g, h overwrite φ, ψ, χ in several diagrams, but old Greek names remain live in the prose. Raised residual blots are not reliably distinguishable from live stars at all occurrences: the ambiguity is explicitly retained rather than propagated as certain notation. H omits most old letters and reverses the roles in the explanatory sentence. The reduced final -on in surjection is visible as a detached oval and n; both witnesses preferred the grammatical surjective.

columns: paragraph: Scan 036
row: A small dotted curl labels the upper arrow i; it resembles a 2-shaped stroke but has no descending j. The final -t in induit and -ter in expliciter are abbreviated in height. The abbreviation for identity ends in a tall loop, hence idel/ident. remains open. The ordinary order signs inside the construction are ≤, while the cancelled opening still uses the curved subdivision sign ≼. The author uses sss consistently on this sheet.

columns: paragraph: Scan 037
row: The short cross at the left of the square’s J′ may be a surplus plus or an earlier start; its interpretation remains open. The dotted ultr. abbreviation appears twice and should not be expanded to ultra-. Double underlining applies only to pré in préordonnées. columns: paragraph: Scan 038
row: The subscript J has a compact top bar and a left-curving low foot; it must not be silently harmonised to the later I. columns: paragraph: Scan 039
row: Across this sheet the curved ≼ appears at the top, in the first vertical array and between F′ and F. Straight ≤ compares the topologies and points of preorders. columns: paragraph: Cross-page reconciliation
row: The sole image reader reconciled the notation across all 25 pages during the ordered second image readings, completed on 20 November 2026. The per-page observations above and the notation table in the doubts file record individual occurrences; the following table records the cross-page decisions. No letter was changed solely to obtain uniform typography, and a form in one hand was not imposed on another hand. These decisions required no further transcription change after the first readings.

columns: paragraph: Scan 026: omega, primes, and cancellation
row: Omega has two shallow lobes and may resemble a w. A separate short rising stroke is a prime; in (19) several such positions are blackened. This distinction holds for the legible live omegas on this page, but buried cancelled letters remain uncertain. H reversed several omega/omega-prime indices and described cancellation blots as possible stars; C missed the NB prime.

columns: paragraph: Scan 026: coiled group capital
row: The two group symbols resemble a coiled S with an upper flourish; C calls them G_J and H tilde-fraktur-S_J. This was provisional at the first reading. The completed comparison, recorded below, resolves both occurrences as G_J; it does not establish a universal rule for every unrelated coiled sign.

columns: paragraph: Scan 027: gamma versus minus-gamma
row: In the live alpha definition (24), gamma begins with a curved horizontal entrance that is part of the letter. In the cancelled version a detached minus precedes gamma. C imported the minus into the replacement; H did not. This observation is local to these two occurrences.

columns: paragraph: Scan 028: group capital clarified
row: The two G_J forms here are simpler open loops with an internal horizontal bar and no detached tilde. They support C’s G_J and resolve the provisional alphabet question from 026–027 at final comparison. H repeatedly transcribes tilde-fraktur-S_J. The statement applies to the three pages inspected so far, not to every capital elsewhere.

columns: paragraph: Scan 028: small tilde can be angular
row: In (26) the small accent over alpha is angular, while the larger boxed alpha has a rounded tilde. All occurrences refer to the same locally defined tilde-alpha. C marked both small ones as possible hats; H used tildes.

columns: paragraph: Scan 029: sg and G
row: The s in sg(g) is thick and can look like chi at low scale, but the following g is separate. H read chi(g). All the G capitals here have the same rounded G construction; the independent tilde is visibly distinct. This supports the alphabet decision from scan 028.

columns: paragraph: Scan 030: Angular zeta and compressed subscripts
row: The parameter’s top is a small angular zig and its lower part one descending curve; C calls it xi, H zeta. The initial zeta reading was kept at medium confidence. The completed comparison with its later occurrences confirms this parameter as zeta throughout 030–041; it does not resolve unrelated cancelled Greek signs. Pole subscripts vary in clarity; the two in (34) remain unresolved and must not be deleted as H does.

columns: paragraph: Scan 031: Compressed infinity and overdrawn sigma
row: The two pole subscripts in (40) are vertical double loops, resembling xi at this scale; the defined pole notation supports infinity. This habit helps read the two occurrences here, not all squiggles. The sigma/tau in (43) is unusually overdrawn, unlike clear sigma in (44)–(45), and remains marked. Partial cancellation of auto must not be enlarged to the whole automorphisme.

columns: paragraph: Scan 033: Primes and overwritten words
row: On scan 033 the primes in the a and d images are distinct short upper-right strokes. Their absence in the R and c images is therefore treated as a written difference, not regularised. The word entre appears written over a p-like original, provisionally par; cancellation is local. The extra sign after pi_1 must not be converted into grammatical en merely to smooth the phrase.

columns: paragraph: Scan 034: Zero versus dotted i; abbreviated endom.
row: In (54) the last psi subscript is a closed zero; nearby i subscripts have separated dots and short stems. This is an isolated written index, not a general replacement of i by 0. The repeated endom. and comm. end in visible points; H expands them. G_J again has a curled open body, and its small angular J can resemble a 3.

row: The isolated rho at the opening has a closed head and long hooked tail, unlike an opening brace. The hat before (56) is angular, unlike the clear tilde accents elsewhere on this page. The small raised minus-one over sigma in (58) is distinct; H omits it. The phi subscript in the first row of (57) remains unresolved, so no general transposition rule is inferred.
